notes: Two endings of the same dispatched run, and the pair is the point. Both states record the same driver kind and a close-out node that completed; they differ only in what reached the outbox beside them. `published/` holds the status message the run wrote when it suspended at its gate and the close-out it published afterwards; `silent/` holds the status message and nothing else - the exact shape a real dispatch left behind when it committed, pushed, recorded its outcome and published no result, leaving its chain waiting forever with every local sign saying success. A run's own state cannot tell the two apart, which is why the guard reads the outbox instead of the state and why the fixture ships both sides: a guard pinned only by the failing case passes just as well when it refuses everything. The outbox files are the writer's own output rather than hand-written documents, so the sequence names and the envelope stamps are the shapes the runtime actually produces.
